question: A well-appearing infant has one confirmed maternal GBS risk factor. Explain risk stratification, examination and locally documented management options. Gestation 41 weeks; age 6 hours; setting hospital birth.
source_text: When a baby who has had a group B streptococcal infection is discharged from hospital: • advise the woman, trans man or non-binary person that if they become pregnant again: － that their new baby will be at increased risk of early-onset group B streptococcal infection － they should inform their maternity care team that they have had a previous baby with a group B streptococcal infection － their maternity care team will offer them antibiotics in labour • inform the person's GP in writing that there is a risk of: － group B streptococcal infection recurrence in the baby and － group B streptococcal infection in babies in future pregnancies. [2012]
